methodological_rigor.justification: The design is a retrospective, exploratory multi-omics reanalysis of a single cBioPortal cohort (n=90) with limited external GEO validation; no sample size justification or power calculation is reported. Feature selection relies on two-group t-tests across tens of thousands of CpG sites, genes, and proteins without any explicit multiplicity correction (FDR/BH), despite p<0.001 thresholds — this inflates false discovery. Correlation thresholds (|r|≥0.7, ≥0.75) are chosen without justification or stability analysis, and there is no cross-validation of the connectome clusters, no held-out test set, and no survival/time-to-event analysis despite the recurrence endpoint. Confounders (age, sex, extent of resection, radiotherapy, Simpson grade, NF2 status) are not adjusted for. The authors themselves acknowledge the absence of survival analysis and predictive performance metrics in the Discussion.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a retrospective exploratory biomarker discovery study using a convenience cohort of 90 patients from cBioPortal with GEO-based 'validation,' consistent with Oxford CEBM level 4 (low-quality cohort / case series-like design). Recurrence and WHO grade are used as surrogate endpoints without time-to-event analysis or predictive metrics (AUC, calibration), limiting direct clinical actionability. The findings nominate candidate biomarkers (LINC01397, CHN2, FAM181A-AS1) with plausible but speculative translational relevance; no functional validation or prospective testing is provided, and the authors concede validation in larger prospective cohorts is required before clinical use.

reporting_quality.justification: REMARK is the most applicable standard given the biomarker/prognostic framing. Reporting falls short on multiple REMARK items: no clear patient flow diagram, incomplete description of inclusion/exclusion for the 90 matched patients, no reporting of follow-up duration, missing baseline clinicopathological covariates, no handling of missing data, and no multivariable modeling or discrimination/calibration metrics. The methods section is terse and some figure captions (Figures 4–6) appear duplicated and inconsistent with the text. Data availability is moderate — primary data come from cBioPortal and GEO (public repositories), but no analytic code, package versions beyond R 4.4.1, parameter files, or scripts are shared, limiting reproducibility.

novelty_literature.justification: The conceptual novelty — applying a 'network connectome' framing borrowed from neuroscience to multi-omics meningioma data — is largely rhetorical, as the underlying method is standard correlation-based multi-omics network/module analysis (akin to WGCNA/iCluster), which has been extensively applied in cancer genomics. Empirical novelty is modest: candidate hub LINC01397 and genes like CHN2, FAM181A-AS1 are reported as novel in meningioma, but LEPR and KCNMA1 have prior links to meningioma (cited refs 17–18). The authors do not clearly differentiate their methodology from prior multi-omics meningioma subtyping work (Bayley 2022, Choudhury 2022, Patel 2019), which they cite but do not benchmark against. Overall this is incremental extension rather than a methodological or biological breakthrough.

writing_presentation.justification: The abstract and introduction are readable, but the Results and figure captions are confusing and inconsistent — Figures 2 and 3 captions describe overlapping PCA/heatmap content, and Figures 4, 5, and 6 captions contain near-verbatim duplicated text that does not match figure numbering in the Results narrative. The Methods are sparse (e.g., iCluster parameters, GO enrichment tool, GEO accession numbers not specified). Terminology (DMR vs CpG site, 'connectome' vs correlation network) is used loosely. Discussion is generally coherent but repeats speculative language without quantitative anchoring; several sentences lack spaces around punctuation (e.g., 'TERTpromoter').

key_strengths: Integrates three matched omics layers (methylation, RNA-seq, proteomics) in the same 90-patient cohort
Attempts external replication using 13 public GEO datasets with concordant trends for several candidates (CHN2, SYNPO2, GSTM5, KCNMA1, LEPR)
Nominates a potentially novel meningioma hub (LINC01397) worth future mechanistic study
Transparent acknowledgment of key limitations (no survival analysis, surrogate endpoints)
key_concerns: No multiple-testing correction described despite genome-wide t-tests across >45,000 features
No survival/time-to-event analysis, no predictive performance (AUC, calibration), no multivariable adjustment for confounders (age, extent of resection, NF2, radiotherapy)
Arbitrary correlation thresholds (0.7/0.75) without stability or sensitivity analyses, and no cross-validation of connectome clusters
Methodological framing as 'connectome' is largely rhetorical; no benchmarking against established multi-omics integration methods (WGCNA, MOFA, SNF)
Duplicated/inconsistent figure captions (Figures 4–6) and sparse methods reduce clarity and reproducibility
No analytic code or scripts shared; parameter settings for iCluster, GO enrichment, and GEO dataset accessions not reported
chief_reviewer.rationale: Exploratory multi-omics reanalysis of a small public cohort with limited statistical rigor, surrogate endpoints, and rhetorical rather than substantive methodological novelty — appropriate for a Tier 4 journal only after major revisions addressing multiplicity correction, confounding, survival analysis, and figure/method clarity.
